commit.message:
i #73 add license headers and news

Add license headers to new function files,
update news of new file organization, and removes
the context of identity.R previous name.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #73 improve API organization

Create new .R files and organize functions around by
their different purpose in the package. Also renamed
string.R to identity.R to clarify its purpose.

DESCRIPTION also now includes ORCID.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #72 improve identity to pass all tests

Several modifications performed to improve identity.
All tests now pass. For details, see the various tests
in tests/testthat/test-string.R

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #38 adds testthat and identity tests

Add several tests for different formats of name in
mailing list and git. All tests names and emails have
been modified to preserve the test case but also respect
the privacy of each person, including the domain of the
email if not a generic domain like gmail.
Current identity fails several
of these tests, and an improved identity function which
pass all tests will be send on a follow commit.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #62 add git interface functions

Functions to obtain a project's git_head(), and perform
git_checkout() were added. These are necessary to perform
interval static analysis over time for parse_line_metrics()
and parse_dependencies() for example.

Minor corrections were applied to README.md, and one interval
function was made public to be facilitate usage in vignettes
of interval analysis.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #60 adds identification of line types

A wrapper for universal ctags was added and
associated vignette. The wrapper simplifies the output
table by providing a csv table and header to the output
of universal ctags.

Setup was added to README.md and a minimal vignette was
added showcasing the wrapper function call interaction
to existing config files.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #59 add file line metrics

A wrapper parser for SCC was added to calculate
lines of code, lines of comment, etc. See
https://github.com/boyter/scc for details.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #57 adds gitlog parser for java refactorings

The new parser function,
parse_java_code_refactoring_json() wraps the
Refactoring Miner tool:
https://github.com/tsantalis/RefactoringMiner#running-refactoringminer-from-the-command-line

A new config for tomcat.yml, a java project, has been added.

See vignettes/refactoringminer_showcase.Rmd for example usage.
README.md has been updated to reflect the usage of configs on vignettes.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #58 add author-committer networks

parse_gitlog() now includes a mode to parse
author-committer networks. Some projects may not
store this data.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #56 Refactor identity assignment

Code logic to assign identity to the network tables
for node and edges no longer depends on igraph, and
was added to the functions on R/string.R

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #54 enable use of git log --grep --perl-regexp

For very large git log analysis like Chromium in
which the log of interest is a much smaller subset,
for example a subset of security bugs or CVEs, being
able to use --grep makes the analysis viable.

The parse_gitlog() function now uses the git log --grep
interface to only provide the log containing the issues
of interest, considerably reducing its size and make it
suitable for analysis in R.

parse_gitlog() now accepts a new parameter containing a
perl regex. This uses a different set of parameters,
only including the master branch instead of all branches.

If the extra perl_expr parameter is not used, the function
will have its prior behavior including all branches for
exploration.

To highlight the discussion of vulnerabilities, as the
data is not present in every project, a new vignette dedicated
for git log and vulnerabilities parsing was created.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #52 make configs more reusable

External tools are now specified on tools.yml. The
parameters of the tools are still project specific,
as we want to encourage reproducibility.

Vignettes and batch script were updated to reflect the change
in configs accordingly.

Data on configs is now assumed to be on a gitignored folder named
rawdata. Provided this convention is respected, config files should
be fully reusable for each project after the 3 line tools.yml is set
up in a different machine.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #53 fix RMD Check Notes and Warnings

Several minor changes across the entire codebase were
made to address Notes and Warnings generated by the
R CMD Check. Changes adressed missing explicit import
of functions, lack of a given parameter on the function
documentation, and perhaps most importantly the
data.table problem with syntax.

See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/data.table/vignettes/datatable-importing.html
for details.

As of this commit, the only note being generated concerns the conf folder
and other files which reside on the top-level, which is a quick-fix.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #51 adds nvd parser and cwe-cve-file networks

NVD feeds can now be parsed to augment cveid-file networks
obtained using parse_commit_message_id_network().

See gitlog_showcase.Rmd for an example of usage on
OpenSSL networks.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #50 refactor config files taxonomy

Updates taxonomy of the config files for clarity and
to prepare for dv8 parameters.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #49 Externalize dependency types on config

The dependency types of interest can now be
specified directly on the config file of
each project, and will automatically be
used by vignettes/depends_showcase.Rmd

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #46 add commit message id coverage metric

Adds `commit_message_id_coverage()` to get
the number of commits which contain an id of interest
such as issue-id or cve-id. An example of usage can be
found on the vignette gitlog_showcase.Rmd

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #46 adds commit message parser

A new parser function, `parse_commit_message_id_network()`
was added. It can be used to extract issue-ids, cve-ids, or
virtually any other id specified on the config file.

The vignette gitlog_showcase.Rmd includes has been extended
to show the CVE-file network leveraging this function.

`parse_gitlog()` was also modified to provide commit_messages
in order to use the new function.

Vignettes were also updated to use filters consistently based
of the config file (see issue i #30 for details on filters).

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #43 less column names assumptions

some functions now requires an additional parameter
to specify the column name needed to realize its
purpose.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #12 Add missing license header

The entire package was already licensed under MPL 2.0.
This just adds a missing header.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #47 add static callgraph for R

This is a built in R call graph parser, which relies
on base R functions to parse the Abstract Syntax Tree.

The 3 added functions parse_rfile_ast(),
parse_r_function_definition(), and
parse_r_function_dependencies() allows to parse individual
 R files and entire packages if provided the filepath.

It is also possible, and my main interest, using the 3
added functions to create a directed weighted graph
containing only the functions defined in the package.
Without any additional pre-processing,
parse_r_function_dependencies() will include every function
call used down to functions such as `c()`.

A vignette will added in a follow commit showcasing how to use
these functions, and more refactoring is likely to follow.
Nonetheless, the available 3 functions are functional.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #20 fixes 0 churn and add new churn functions

The churn metric function task was simplified to only
calculate churn. Several other tasks such as filtering
for a given interval, parsing commit dates from hashes,
etc, were separated in various other functions.

In doing so, it was observed the heuristics being
calculated before sorting, and applied after sorting
were leading to some inconsistency on the results,
as the elements that should be filtered were shuffled.

This was addressed when each heuristic, and filtering
by time interval was separated by functions.

See vignettes/interval_and_metric_showcase.Rmd for
details on how to use the new functions.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #44 create minimal interface for intervals

R/interval.R was added as a general function
to calculate metrics over a sequence of commit
intervals.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #30 add filters for file and filepaths

The R/parsers.R api now contains 2 new functions,
filter_by_file_extension() and filter_by_filepath_substring().
These functions can be used to filter rows from
parse_gitlog() and parse_dependencies(), and in the future
the R/metrics.R api to provide more control on the files
analyzed.

Config files now includes 2 additional parameters which
provides input for these 2 functions directly, however
the functions can still be used without the config file.

Cross-referencing was added to the parser_*, parser_*_network,
and filter functions. When using for example ?parse_gitlog
the function docs will now suggest "See Also" with a clicable
link to functions of the same family or suggesting functions
to obtain a non-obvious parameter (e.g. the filter functions
to the parse_functions).

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #41 Add conf file to NEWS.md

Adds mention to config files to NEWS.md

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #41 Creates conf file format

The package now suggests the use of yaml to create
config files. The dependency is optional: The package
API does not assume config files being passed around.
Rather, the vignette showcases how the .yml file is
parsed.

The config files will be more useful when a cli is
defined for the package, or to share project configs
around. Note the files are not fully reusable as it is,
because the end-user still has to specify the path for
any external dependencies.

Nonetheless, I expect as more functionality is added,
other parameters will still justify keeping the config
files. Such as Depends need to specify a language,
bug density metrics needing to specify commit hashes,
file filtering based on extensions or certain regex,
or even identity matching approach for cli.

This commit also adds to parser functions a path
expansion, which allows for config files to include
relative paths using ~, e.g. ~/Desktop.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #26 add pkgdown to NEWS.md

Includes a mention for the pkgdown docs on NEWS.md

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #26 Add pkgdown page to repo

Code documentation has been added to parse_(),
parse_*_network() and assign_exact_match().
Pkgdown website has also been defined using
the existing vignettes and the provided API
documentation.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #40 add timestamp parsing and bipartite

Add to the other parse_*_network functions the
timestamp parsing wih POSIXct and bipartite
column.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #6 add examples and overview to README.md

Provide more examples commonly expected to be found
on a README.md

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #39 remove mailinglist example from gitlog

This should have been removed previously when
mailinglist_showcase.Rmd vignette was created.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #31 add assign_exact_identity

Adds function assign_exact_identity to compare if name_email
pairs within gitlogs, within mailing lists, and between gitlogs
and mailing lists belong to the same person.

This reduces threats to validity in which nodes from
parse_gitlog_network() and parse_mailinglist_network()
are considered different, when they are the same person
using a slight different name or email (but not both)
over time. Provided at least either change incrementally,
this function should be able to identify all as the same
person.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #36 Add CONTRIBUTION.md

Some details for the long run concerning signing commits.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #37 add NEWS.md

To facilitate changes to the codebase, as the number
of issues are now a bit large.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #35 add logo to the project

Adds a logo to the README.md for the project. The
image is slightly modified from a page of "Kunstformen
der Natur" (Art Forms in Nature) by German biologist
Ernst Haeckel. It is made available on Public Domain
by the Library of Congress (www.loc.gov) at:

https://www.rawpixel.com/image/2272232/free-illustration-image-vintage-sea-ernst-haeckel

Signed-off-by: Carlos Paradis <carlosviansi@gmail.com>

i #33 Removes gitlog overhead from parser

After further experimentation of Perceval interface,
it seems the git command can be executed for local repos.
The readme example first suggests it was for online repos only.
Thus, this commit removes the unecessary step of generating a
git log in order to parse the git repo of interest.
i #6 minor fix on unecessary step
i #6 updates setup and examples

i #22 fixes accidental project path changes

When removing .git, only the last ocurrence
of the term should be removed. It was possible
before this commit that, if the word git appeared
in the project path, it would also be removed.
i #25 fix leaking parameter

i #24 rename vignettes for consistency

Vignettes were renamed to reflect the different
data showcase. Also, the mailing list portion
was split from the original vignette since it
does not concern gitlogs.

i #23 adds lang identifier and file filter

Adds a suggestion for the package gh to use
on this Vignette. The provided endpoint will
obtain the language percent of a project given
it's URL on Github. A language must be chosen
in order to use Depends.

A rudimentary string matching filter was added to
filter out file_paths which contain `test` and
`__init__.py` on the vignette only.

i #8 Adds Depends bash interface

Depends (https://github.com/multilang-depends/depends) can now
be used to import file-file dependencies. See the associated
project for more information on the type of dependencies.

Two functions are made available on this commit:

parse_dependencies() converts Depends json file into a
.csv table, containing all types of dependencies detected
by Depends.

parse_dependencies_network() leverages the .csv to create
a weighted edgelist which can be used by graph software
to visualize dependenies. The function is paramaterize
the types of interest, and calculate their sum as weight.

vignettes/depends_showcase.Rmd provide sample code on how
to visualize it using igraph and VisNetwork R packages.

i #12 Add MPL 2.0 License

As of this commit, the code only Imports the
following packages:

 * data.table (MPL 2.0)
 * stringi (BSD-3-clause)
 * jsonlite (Apache 2.0)

Moreover, the use of Perceval (GPL 3.0) is done by command line,
and can be replaced by any other commit log or mailing list log parsers,
as will be done in future commits. This, to the best of my knowledge,
as I am not a lawyer, complies with GPL based on:

https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html#MereAggregation

and other open source packages like XGBoost (i #1338), in respect
to clarify the  codebase does not depend on a particular GPL project
to function.

Author roles were also rectified.

i #14 Remove igraph dependency

R/parsers.R no longer generate igraph objects,
but instead nodes/edgelist tables which can then
be exported for Gephi, VisNetwork, RCy3, etc which
have more permissive licenses. The nodes/edgelist
format is also standard practice.

The lubridate package was also removed from Suggests,
since just use base POSIXct since prior commits to
remove lubridate dependencies.

i #21 replace stringr with stringi

Remove dependency from stringr due to GPL license
requirements. Also adds additional imports to other
R files to correct my misconception a single file
would apply to everything.

Some vignettes still contained library(), they have been
replaced with require().

i #15 add forgotten mbox export

parse_mbox_igraph() was left out. Fixed on this commit.

i #13 Remove lubridate references

All lubridate:: calls have been replaced by
built-in POSIXct class. The behavior should
be identical.

i #15 Fixes namespace to imports

Removing the packages from Depends on DESCRIPTION
required adding @importsFrom and @export across all
functions, hence this commit slightly modifies the
entire codebase.

Vignettes were edited to require() instead of attaching
using library() following best practies.

Rather than copy and paste data.table across all functions,
I followed XGBoost package approach and loaded only on a
single file. Since all codebase wont work without parsers,
that seem the most logical place. Other more situational
dependence on functions will use the typical :: approach
which is hard for data.table.

Arguably data.table could belong on Depends, but even the
package maintainer argues against it, see:

https://github.com/Rdatatable/data.table/issues/3076

i #19 Adds churn metrics

A .R file for churn and future metrics were added.
The vignettes/churn_metrics.Rmd provide usage examples.

i #18 Adds serialization to logs

Adds serialization to git log objects, sometimes raw
data >= 1GB.

i #9 move parsed gitlog table responsibility

Currently, parse_gitlog_igraph is responsible to
transform the json into a simple table. This commit
moves the responsibility to parse_gitlog instead.

i #6 Cite live example and vignette

README.md updated to refer to vignette and website
for how to use the code.

i #5 Adds commit and co-change networks

Function parse_gitlog_igraph now has 2 modes ("author","commit")
as parameter. The already existing contribution network (author-file)
can be obtained using the mode "author".

The new mode, "commit", creates a commit-file network. In the vignette
vignettes/network_parsers.Rmd the graph is plotted, and a projection is
created to generate the adjacency matrix.

i #4 fixes communication graph as weighted

The edgelists are now grouped into a weight column,
such that is_weighted(apr_communication_network) == TRUE.

I.e. igraph's graph properly recognize an author may contribute
to an e-mail thread multiple times.

i #1 Adds gitlog network parser

Another function is added to use Perceval output and
make a contribution network interactive visualization.

Note this function properly outputs a weighted network,
as the same dev can contribute to the same file multiple
times. I.e. is_weighted(apr_git_network) == TRUE.

This should be fixed on the communication network in a following
commit.

i #4 adds igraph as package dependency

Since igraph is now part of the defined functions,
it should also be on the list of dependencies.

visNetwork, the package required to plot the
interactive plots in the vignette, is listed as a suggestion.

i #4 Add communication network parser and viz

The vignette was renamed to showcase various networks.

The mbox_downloader.sh was provided by Wolfgang. In a future
issue, this should be integrated into R code for full automation.

R/parsers.R have 2 new functions to use Perceval to parse mbox,
and to use the parsed mbox into an igraph object were added.
The vignette  uses the igraph object to create a
interactive visualization of the data.

i #1 Add contribution network parser

This adds a function that automates the execution of
MetricsGrimmoire Percerval tool:

https://github.com/chaoss/grimoirelab-perceval

And provides the basic code for the R package. See README.md
for details.
